verdict.rationale: Graphite documents a "codebase-aware" AI review agent and a Chat feature that can find related files, understand dependencies, and pull context from other PRs. That plausibly helps a reviewer grasp large changes within a repository. Nothing in the evidence shows coherent review of a single change spanning multiple repositories: the multi-repo item is an inbox filter, and stacking is a way to split work rather than a way to understand it. Missing for 10: explicit cross-repository change correlation and review, documented monorepo-scale context handling, and independent or hands-on corroboration of codebase-aware review quality on large codebases.
